verification.note: migrated from data/antibiogram-raw.json: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026)

notes: Padmaja et al., Bioinformation 21(6):1475-1480 (2025), KIMS Amalapuram ICU (MICU/SICU/CCIU), Jun 2023-Jul 2024. Text-extractable PDF (PyMuPDF), 6 pages. Source reports susceptibility ONLY as qualitative bands: highly sensitive >=80%, moderately sensitive 60-80%, poorly sensitive <60% (Table 3, page 4). No S/I/R counts, no exact per-drug percentages EXCEPT Tobramycin vs Acinetobacter = 96% (only exact figure printed). For 60-80% bands I stored midpoint s=70 with approx:true; for <60% bands I left s=null and used qualitative q (no lower bound given, so a number would be a guess); for the single 'carbapenems strong 80%' Pseudomonas statement I stored s=80 approx. 'Carbapenems' is a class - only meropenem was tested (methods: 'Meropenem and minocycline used as reserved drugs'), so mapped to meropenem with note. 'Cephalosporins (1st-3rd gen)' is a class - recorded as ceftazidime + ceftriaxone (the named first-line cephalosporins) with note. Cefoperazone-sulbactam and ceftazidime-avibactam kept as printed combo tokens (not plain cefoperazone/ceftazidime). n values are Table-2 TOTAL ICU isolate counts per genus (E.coli 244, Klebsiella 277, Pseudomonas 148, Acinetobacter 93, Proteus 13); T
issues: This is a banded/qualitative antibiogram, not numeric. Table 3 gives ranges (>=80% highly, 60-80% moderately, <60% poorly). The extraction represents the 60-80% band as s=70 (midpoint) and flags approx=true; the 80% cell (Pseudomonas carbapenems) as s=80; and <60% cells as s=null. This is a defensible modeling choice but no exact percentages exist in the source except Tobramycin/Acinetobacter (96%

SOURCE INTERNAL CONFLICT (E. coli, cefoperazone-sulbactam): Table 3 lists cefoperazone-sulbactam under E. coli's <60% (poorly sensitive) column, but the page-3 narrative states 'cefoperazone-sulbactam, other reserved agents such as carbapenems and minocycline exhibited moderate sensitivity (60-80%)' for E. coli. The extraction followed Table 3 (s=null, <60%), which is the correct primary tabular s

SOURCE INTERNAL CONFLICT (Klebsiella, nitrofurantoin): Table 3 lists Nitrofurantoin as the effective urinary drug for Klebsiella, but page-3 narrative says 'nitrofurantoin showed low sensitivity.' Extraction followed Table 3 (effective) and explicitly documents the conflict. Acceptable.

SOURCE INTERNAL CONFLICT (Pseudomonas & Acinetobacter urinary agents): Table 3 lists Nitrofurantoin+Norfloxacin as effective urinary drugs for both Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter, and page-4 narrative agrees ('effective against Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter'), yet page-3 narrative says these agents 'showed inadequate sensitivity'/'demonstrated limited efficacy' for these organisms. MINOR over-specification: the paper names organisms only at genus level for the ICU cohort (Klebsiella, Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, Proteus). The extraction assigns species (K. pneumoniae, P. aeruginosa, A. baumannii, P. mirabilis). These are reasonable inferences (species named elsewhere in discussion) but are not stated for the antibiogram itself. No susceptibility impact.

All n values, band assignments, and drug mappings verified correct against Table 2 and Table 3. Meropenem <60% for Acinetobacter (explicit in Table 3 poorly-sensitive column), Tobramycin 96% for Acinetobacter, and Pseudomonas carbapenems 80% are all accurately captured. No hallucinated cells and no %R<->%S direction errors.
